- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct downward quickly — overcorrects or lags in adjusting to new equilibrium.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model holds high forecasts longer than actual price tends to revert toward recent average.
- Forecast bias is more pronounced in the second half of the 30-day window — model underestimates later days, especially when true values show downward drift.
- Model reacts too slowly to recent price drops — fails to recognize momentum shifts or policy-driven corrections.
- When history shows strong upward momentum, model often fails to anticipate the peak and overestimates continuation.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility — underestimates short-term volatility spikes and overestimates long-term trends.
- Forecast horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are consistently biased high, especially when recent prices are trending upward.
